subject: obstetrics-gynaecology
title: Disorders of amniotic fluid: oligo, polyhydramnios and amnioinfusion

steps.tx: Normal **amniotic fluid** at term measures five hundred to one thousand millilitres, turned over by fetal swallowing and urination, with an amniotic fluid index of five to twenty five centimetres and a deepest vertical pocket of two to eight centimetres. Too little fluid with an index under five or a pocket under two centimetres defines oligohydramnios, often from growth restriction, ruptured membranes, renal agenesis of the Potter type, post maturity or angiotensin converting enzyme inhibitors. Low fluid squeezes the cord and causes decelerations.
steps.say: Amniotic fluid normally totals five hundred to one thousand millilitres near term, renewed by fetal swallowing and urine output, and ultrasound gives an index of five to twenty five centimetres or a deepest pocket of two to eight. Oligohydramnios means an index under five or a pocket under two, most often from growth restriction, ruptured membranes, absent kidneys, post maturity or certain drugs. Too little fluid compresses the cord, so growth, Dopplers and the heart rate pattern need surveillance.

steps.tx: In **oligohydramnios** the ultrasound shows a small pocket beside the fetal abdomen with a deepest vertical pocket of one point two centimetres, below the normal lower limit, and the four quadrant depths sum to an amniotic fluid index of zero point nine centimetres, which is also low. Both measurements therefore confirm oligohydramnios, and the finding raises concern for cord compression. Management needs surveillance of growth and fluid volume, so that delivery can be timed safely for mother and baby.
steps.say: This ultrasound measures fluid in oligohydramnios: the caliper gives a deepest vertical pocket of one point two centimetres and the inset adds four quadrants to an index of zero point nine, both below the normal range. Low fluid matters because the umbilical cord can be compressed during contractions, producing decelerations. The next steps are to confirm membrane status, assess growth and Dopplers, and keep surveillance close until delivery timing becomes clear.

vis.alt: Obstetric ultrasound shows a small fluid pocket by the fetal abdomen with DVP and four quadrant AFI measurements below the normal range.
vis.caption: Ultrasound showing oligohydramnios with low DVP and AFI measurements, Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: Too much fluid defines **polyhydramnios** with an index over twenty five centimetres or a pocket over eight centimetres, caused by diabetes, fetal anomalies such as anencephaly, tracheo oesophageal fistula and duodenal atresia with a double bubble, twin to twin transfusion in the recipient, hydrops and macrosomia. The overdistended uterus causes pressure and breathlessness, preterm labour, malpresentation, cord prolapse and atonic postpartum bleeding. Oral glucose testing, a detailed anomaly scan and haemoglobin A1c help find the cause, while mild idiopathic cases can be observed.
steps.say: Polyhydramnios means an index above twenty five centimetres or a deepest pocket above eight, and the diagram shows common causes from diabetes to duodenal atresia with its double bubble. Excess fluid stretches the uterus, causing breathlessness and pressure, and raises risks of preterm labour, unstable lie, cord prolapse and atonic bleeding after delivery. Assessment includes glucose testing, a careful anomaly scan and haemoglobin A1c, while mild cases without a cause can simply be observed.

vis.alt: Diagram illustrating polyhydramnios with a fetus in excessive amniotic fluid. Insets show anencephaly and duodenal atresia (double bubble sign), common causes. Fetal malpresentation is also depicted.
vis.caption: Polyhydramnios: excessive fluid, causes, and complications

steps.tx: Manage **oligohydramnios** with hydration, transcervical amnioinfusion of saline for variable decelerations, and delivery at thirty six to thirty seven weeks when isolated at term, earlier with growth restriction or abnormal Dopplers, and steroids when preterm. For polyhydramnios, selected preterm cases may receive indomethacin, amnioreduction relieves pressure and breathlessness, and delivery is planned near thirty seven to thirty eight weeks once diabetes and anomalies are excluded. Malpresentation may need caesarean section, and cord prolapse needs knee chest positioning and urgent delivery.
steps.say: For oligohydramnios, maternal hydration, amnioinfusion for recurring variable decelerations and planned delivery around thirty six to thirty seven weeks are the mainstays, earlier when growth restriction or Dopplers worsen. Polyhydramnios may need indomethacin in selected preterm cases or amnioreduction when pressure and breathlessness are severe, with delivery near thirty seven to thirty eight weeks. Always treat the underlying cause, watch for malpresentation and cord prolapse, and give steroids when preterm delivery threatens.

steps.tx: Twin to twin transfusion syndrome affects **monochorionic** twins when the donor becomes stuck with oligohydramnios and the recipient drowns in polyhydramnios through shared placental vessels. Quintero staging grades severity, fetoscopic laser ablation of connecting vessels treats advanced stages, amnioreduction temporises, and selective reduction is reserved for severe disease. Related conditions include the acardiac pump twin in twin reversed arterial perfusion and anaemia polycythaemia sequence detected by middle cerebral Dopplers. Fortnightly scans from sixteen weeks detect these complications early, and referral to fetal medicine guides laser treatment.
steps.say: In monochorionic twins, unbalanced placental sharing can leave one twin stuck with too little fluid while the other carries too much, the twin to twin transfusion syndrome table summarised beside this step. Quintero stages describe severity, laser ablation seals the connecting vessels, and amnioreduction buys time. Fortnightly scans from sixteen weeks look for this and for anaemia polycythaemia sequence on Dopplers, and early referral to fetal medicine offers fetoscopic treatment when stages advance.
